title: Artificial Intelligence Governance and Non-Proliferation
summary: Public reproducibility layer for applied analysis of AI governance, non-proliferation, institutional process terrain, and multilateral policy using releasable statistical and visualization workflows.

methods.usage: Uses principal coordinates analysis on a structured process-evidence distance matrix to represent similarity among multilateral venues and processes.
Uses deterministic R workflows to reproduce process-terrain coordinates, diagnostics, and a publication-style strategic-terrain visualization.

geography.note: Mapped countries represent explicit portfolio-facing emerging-technology coverage; the public reproducibility layer itself is multilateral rather than a set of national studies.

access.disclosure: This repository is a sanitized public reproducibility layer. It excludes private source archives, evidence packets, working panels, internal notes, and decision-support materials retained in the private working repository.

title: Counterterrorism, Ethnosectarian Context and Islamic State Attack Patterns
summary: Reproducible analysis of Islamic State-linked attack patterns in Iraq using terrorism-event data, district-level ethnosectarian composition, spatial boundaries, population weighting, diagnostics, and statistical modeling.

methods.usage: Links attack events to Iraqi district geography and population-weighted ethnosectarian composition, with spatial validation and visualization.
Uses explicit missingness audits and diagnostic workflows as part of reproducible event-data preparation and interpretation.
Uses modular R workflows, saved analytical objects, diagnostics, and publication-oriented figures to make analytical decisions reproducible.

geography.note: The current repository is centered on district-level empirical analysis in Iraq.

access.disclosure: Public code and derived artifacts are available, while third-party source data remain subject to their original licensing, EULA, citation, and redistribution constraints.

title: UN Transcript Intelligence and Dynamic Voting Alignment
summary: Technical project for reproducible United Nations transcript intelligence, structured evidence extraction, and analysis of changing voting alignment across multilateral processes.

methods.usage: Provides the computational pipeline for collecting, structuring, validating, and linking transcript-derived evidence.
Planned analytical layer represents changing actor alignment and relational structure across time.
Planned longitudinal analysis tracks changes in actor positions and alignment across repeated institutional observations.

geography.note: The project is institution-centered and potentially global; country coverage should be generated from the observed transcript and voting corpus rather than hard-coded.

access.disclosure: The public repository is currently a project shell; substantive data, methodology, code, and empirical results are not yet published there.
